title_en: Interim Provisions on the Management of Unscheduled Flights in Civil Aviation Transport

articles.content_en: For the purpose of safeguarding the national aviation rights and interests, ensuring air transport safety, and promoting the development of civil air transport, these Provisions are formulated.

These Provisions shall apply to the non-scheduled flights of Chinese and foreign civil aircraft engaged in the carriage of passengers, baggage, cargo and mail within the territory of the People's Republic of China and between the People's Republic of China and foreign countries.
For the purposes of these Provisions, "non-scheduled flight" means a civil air transport flight that does not belong to a scheduled flight.

Engaging in non-scheduled flights must apply to the competent civil aviation authority of the State Council, and the flight may be conducted only after approval. The application and approval procedures shall be formulated by the competent civil aviation authority of the State Council.

Engaging in non-scheduled flights must comply with the transport rules formulated by the competent civil aviation authority of the State Council, and shall not affect the normal operation of scheduled flights.

The flight crew and aircraft engaged in non-scheduled flights must meet the conditions or technical standards prescribed by the competent civil aviation authority of the State Council, and must possess crew licenses, aircraft registration certificates, airworthiness certificates, and other certificates and documents that shall be carried according to the relevant provisions.

Where a foreign civil air transport enterprise operates non-scheduled flights that fly into or out of the territory of the People's Republic of China for transport business, the matter shall be handled in accordance with the relevant provisions of the air transport agreement signed between the Government of the People's Republic of China and the government of that foreign country.
A foreign civil air transport enterprise shall not operate the transport business of non-scheduled flights between any two points within the territory of the People's Republic of China.

With respect to non-scheduled flights operated by a foreign civil air transport enterprise for remunerated transport business, the Chinese side shall have the right to charge compensation fees for aviation business rights.
The prices of non-scheduled civil air transport shall be subject to market-regulated prices, which shall be independently formulated by the air transport enterprises.

Article 11 Unless specially approved by the competent civil aviation authority under the State Council, a foreign aircraft engaged in non-remunerated non-scheduled flights may only fly to a designated location within the territory of the People's Republic of China, and shall not carry any persons or cargo other than those originally on board such aircraft out of the territory of the People's Republic of China, nor shall it leave the original persons or cargo within the territory of the People's Republic of China.

Article 12 An aircraft engaged in non-scheduled flights for international transportation must, in accordance with the relevant provisions of the People's Republic of China, go through the formalities of frontier inspection, customs, health quarantine, and security check, etc., and pay the prescribed fees according to regulations.

Article 13 Foreign aircraft engaged in non-scheduled flights, their crew members, and the passengers, baggage, cargo, and mail carried on board, when entering, leaving, or within the territory of the People's Republic of China, must comply with the relevant laws, regulations, and rules of the People's Republic of China, and pay all prescribed fees according to regulations.

Article 14 The operator of a foreign aircraft engaged in non-scheduled flights must take out liability insurance for damage caused to third parties on the ground when such aircraft flies within the territory of the People's Republic of China; if engaged in non-scheduled flights carrying passengers, baggage, cargo, and mail, the operator must also take out statutory liability insurance.

Article 15 With respect to any unit or individual that violates these Provisions, the competent civil aviation authority under the State Council may impose a warning, a fine, order a suspension of flight, or revoke relevant certificates; if a crime is constituted, the judicial organ shall investigate criminal liability according to law.
Article 16 These Provisions shall come into force as of the date of promulgation.
